## Where to start

*Added 2026-07-31 with the V1 re-cut. Four states, so "what next" is a lookup rather than a reconstruction across 300 lines.*

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **▶ Frontier** | Open, unblocked, ready for an agent to pick up **today**. |
| **⏳ Sequenced** | In V1, but waiting on a dependency named in its ticket. |
| **🌫 Fog** | Real work, deliberately not ticketed until its slice starts. |
| **🚧 Gate** | Cannot be cleared by a ticket at all — an owner action or a decision session. |

**▶ The frontier right now** — the Ask MVP's critical path first, because [v1.md](v1.md) names it as the checkpoint inside Phase B:

- **T-281 → T-299 → T-282 → T-283**, then **T-259** — the Lens path. The MVP's terminal wave; depends on none of Wave 2 or Wave 3, and needs no migration.
- **T-251** — revocable sessions. Off the critical path, recommended inside it: a signed cookie cannot be revoked, and that matters the moment this is in front of anyone.
- **T-270** and **T-276** — the two spikes (locator extraction, the authority corpus). Block nothing, unblock Wave 3, and both are research rather than build.

**🚧 The three gates**, none of which a ticket can clear:

1. **The infra/security decision session** — cloud provider, blob storage, hosting, key management, residency, production identity. **Blocks any external pilot.** Pre-reads: [nfr.md](nfr.md) (numbers still a strawman — `Q-027`) and the 2026-07-25 rulings.
2. **The Microsoft CSPP application** — owner-driven; blocks Slice A3 P3 only. P1 shipped, P2 builds against a dev-harness engine regardless.
3. **Four design questions** — `Q-007` and `Q-008` block V1's checker; `Q-012` (notifications) blocks the review cycle being usable in practice; `Q-028` blocks wiring the retrieval scope filter. All in [grill-questions.md](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md).

**V1 vs post-V1.** [v1.md](v1.md) is the authority on what the pilot contains. In summary: **in** — the Ask MVP, Waves 0–5 and 8, the full DMS lifecycle, three organisations, a 100–500 document corpus, three declared workflows, and the new ingest and checker work not yet ticketed. **Out** — the authority corpus (T-276–T-278 beyond the spike), `web_research` (T-279), `verifier` (T-275, T-286), scoping questions (Wave 6), Teach (Wave 7), Slice A3 P2–P4, Slice O P2, and Slices B, E, F, G, H.

## How to read a ticket

`T-###` — title. **Next free number: T-300** — **derive it, don't trust it: `pnpm run check:tickets -- --next`** scans this board, the history *and* `git log` and prints the next free number. Bump this line in the same commit that claims numbers; `pnpm run check` fails if it falls behind, or if one number is defined twice. The line stays because it is readable, but the script is the authority — the prose convention alone let concurrent sessions collide twice (T-208–T-210, T-223–T-233). **Deps:** tickets that must be done first. **Done when:** the acceptance test, drawn from the destination spec its slice serves â [v1.md](v1.md) for current work, [walking-skeleton.md](walking-skeleton.md) for the closed skeleton milestones. Package names from [repo-structure.md](repo-structure.md). A ticket is sized for one focused agent run (roughly a PR each).

**Definition of done, every ticket:** typed against `packages/contracts`; unit-tested; no surface reaches below the API; no code path resolves its own permissions (component 2 rule); lints and builds clean in CI.

## ⚠ One named build-time decision — skeleton auth

The design layer defers real identity/security to the infra/security session (component 1, open). The skeleton still needs a login. **Decision taken for the skeleton, to be superseded by that session:** email + password session login for the seeded users (`POST /auth/session`, httpOnly cookie), plus Entra ID SSO on the Copilot path (M6, where Microsoft mandates it). No self-serve signup, no password reset, no roles beyond what the data model already carries. This is scaffolding, not the security model; it is listed here so it is a recorded choice, not an accident.

**Production identity is committed as Entra-first (recorded 2026-07-04):** most users will arrive through Microsoft Entra (Azure AD), so production login is Entra ID SSO (OIDC) as the primary path, with the skeleton's password login retained only as a break-glass/dev mechanism to be decided at the infra/security session. The build already enables this: identity is established at one API boundary only (T-021/T-023, contracts principle 3), `User.external_identity` carries the Entra subject from Drawer 1, and T-071 exercises the full Entra → User → Participant mapping. Adding web SSO later is an additive login route, not a rework.

## The roadmap after the skeleton (coarse — ticketed when its slice starts)

Ordered by the wedge-first logic of the overview; each slice names its design gate from the [grill tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md). Nothing here is execution-ready by design.

**Slice A3 — Co-authoring & the editing substrate: Infora as a WOPI host, native Office files co-authored in real Microsoft Office** — 🎯 **designed 2026-07-25 (ADR-0043 + amendments to 0034 / 0036 / 0039 / 0041); P1 ticketed (T-220–T-222 — renumbered 2026-07-25: the drafted T-208–T-210 were already taken by Slice S), P2–P4 coarse until the CSPP / engine track is live.** The sandbox becomes a true SharePoint / iManage-style working area: drop a draft, open it in Word / Excel / PowerPoint, co-author, and have edits sync straight back — files never leaving Infora. The incumbent-validated posture (iManage Work co-authoring; NetDocuments CollabSpaces — both keep files in their own DMS and become WOPI hosts, renting Office co-authoring via Microsoft's CSPP). Infora stays the system of record and the ethical-wall authority; the SharePoint-as-substrate route was considered and rejected (per-org tenancy collides with the cross-org wall — ADR-0043). Grounding is untouched (library-only; the sandbox never grounds).

**External dependency (owner-driven, gates go-live not the build):** the **Microsoft CSPP application** — real-Office co-authoring cannot ship until Microsoft approves. The WOPI host (P2) is built and validated against a self-hosted dev-harness engine (Collabora / OnlyOffice) meanwhile, then pointed at Microsoft Office at approval (P3). P1 has no Microsoft dependency and ships regardless.

*P1 — DMS parity (no Microsoft dependency, ship now):* **✅ T-220–T-222 built 2026-07-26** (one verified commit per ticket; api 175/175, e2e 44/44 green). Deviations: rename is **allowed while checked out** (owner-confirmed — a title is author-owned metadata, not canonical content; the T-166 precedent), so only Replace surfaces the head-lock refusal; upload now seeds a genesis ambient revision so a fresh upload reads `v0.1` and the first replace increments to `v0.2`; the `/file` path joins `sandbox-uploads` on the CSRF multipart allowlist (ADR-0044).
- **T-220 — Contracts + API: sandbox document rename + replace-native-file.** Close the two gaps found this session: a sandbox document has no rename path (the PATCH bodies only carry `content` / `authoringMetadata`), and an uploaded file cannot be replaced. Add rename (`title`) — allowed on an unbound document; a bound document's display name stays the container's (ADR-0038). Add `POST /sandbox-documents/:id/file` (multipart) replacing the canonical native file with a new upload of the same format family — writes a new blob + `file_ref`, bumps the working revision; **refused while `head_locked`** (it rewrites canonical content, like the T-122 conversion) and only for `origin='uploaded'`. Durable prior-blob retention is P2 (noted). | *(Deps: T-122, T-166)*
- **T-221 — Surface: rename & replace-file actions in the sandbox drawer.** Per-document row/context actions in the folder view (reusing the T-163 `Modal`): **Rename** (text field) and **Replace file…** (file picker, `origin='uploaded'` only), each surfacing the head-lock refusal cleanly; the row shows format + last-updated. No `window.prompt`, semantic tokens only (the standing A2.1 acceptance tests). | *(Deps: T-220, T-163)*
- **T-222 — P1 acceptance e2e.** Upload a docx → rename it → replace it with a new docx (working revision increments, history shows it) → check out (freeze) → replace is refused while locked → release → replace succeeds. | *(Deps: T-220, T-221)*

*P2 — the WOPI host + embedded co-authoring* **(coarse — ticketed when the engine track starts).** Migration for the WOPI item/lock refs (reusing `head_locked` / `sandbox_checkout_events`) and the `file_ref` pointer extension; the WOPI host endpoints (`CheckFileInfo` / `GetFile` / `PutFile` / lock) with access gated by `sandbox_scope_grants`; `PutFile` → a `v0.x` ambient working revision (ADR-0041); the embedded editor pane in the sandbox drawer; the dev-harness engine (Collabora / OnlyOffice) provisioned as the first real infra dependency (ADR-0037 / the infra session). Acceptance: open → co-edit → save-back → new working version, plus the wall negative (revoke drops editor access in-transaction).

*P3 — CSPP → real Microsoft Office* **(coarse; gated on the CSPP approval).** Swap the P2 dev-harness engine for genuine Microsoft Office for the web behind the same WOPI host; desktop co-authoring is a later CSPP milestone.

*P4 — the Infora agent as an Office Add-in* **(coarse; converges with Slice B below).** The task-pane Add-in that grounds against the **library** from inside Office via `groundedLibrary(slice)` — the draft (read from Office.js) fused with the grounded record, in one surface. Shares its surface with Slice B's Word add-in; design not settled (ADR-0043 open item).

**Slice O — The document ontology: classification vocabulary + first-class relationships** — 🎯 **designed 2026-07-26 (ADR-0045; grill session O); Drawer 6 drawn ([data-model.md](data-model.md)); P1 ✅ built 2026-07-26 (T-240–T-244; renumbered from the drafted T-223–T-227, which collided with concurrent UI/polish commits T-223–T-233 — a T-234–T-239 gap is left for other live sessions), P2 coarse until the Engine track is live.** Built on branch `slice-o-document-ontology` in an isolated worktree (the repo had multiple live sessions); one verified commit per ticket, migration 0031, verified against an isolated DB (db 21/21, api 7/7, knowledge 26/26, e2e 7/7 incl. the wall and the plan-surface render). Over the flat library sits a legible model of *how documents relate* (component 5): a Uniclass 2015 / ISO 19650 classification vocabulary the library owner owns, and typed relationship edges between containers. Colocated relational tables, derived not duplicated (ADR-0024/0045) — so the retrieval path gains a **semantic pre-filter** in the same query as the access+state pre-filter (ADR-0022), the lever that scopes a 100k-document corpus before a single embedding is compared. Agent-facing first with a thin confirmation surface (classification an editable field, edges agent-proposed/human-confirmed — ADR-0045 Fork 3). Grounding is untouched (the ontology is metadata and structure, never a grounded corpus — ADR-0011/0021).

*P1 — the ontology substrate + retrieval pre-filter (no Engine dependency, ship now):*
- **T-240 — Data-model Drawer 6 + migration + seed: the classification vocabulary and relationship-edge tables.** Drawn (Drawer 6). Write the migration for `classification_facet`, `classification_term` (hierarchical, currency-by-state), `container_classification` (mutable, agent-proposed/human-editable), `document_relationship` (append-only, propose-then-confirm, currency-by-state). Seed Infora's default Uniclass 2015 / ISO 19650 facets + terms and **copy them per project at creation** (mirror the acceptance-code seed, ADR-0003/0045). Contracts types. | *(Deps: the acceptance-code copy-per-project seed — T-115 precedent)*
- **T-241 — Contracts + API: classify a container; propose / confirm / retire edges.** Set and edit a container's classification per facet (agent-proposed values allowed, human-editable); create an edge (proposed, no effect), confirm an edge (human-confirm → live), retire an edge (currency-by-state, never deleted). Reads: a container's classification + edges; a project's facet/term vocabulary. Access-resolved (component 2) — edges and classification ride the deliverable-visibility pre-filter (Drawer 5); no path resolves its own permissions. | *(Deps: T-240)*
- **T-242 — Retrieval: the semantic pre-filter.** Extend the grounding/retrieval query (ADR-0022/0024) so a scoped retrieval pre-filters by classification facet/term and by edge-connected containers *in the same statement* as the existing access+state pre-filter — the 100k-doc scoping lever; add the classification slice params to `groundedLibrary(slice)`. Structural-only reads (currency / coverage / dependency) answer from the tables with no vector search. | *(Deps: T-240; existing retrieval T-012/T-033/T-054)* **⚠ Note 2026-07-31 — substrate only, no selector.** The SQL pre-filter is built and tested, but nothing populates it: `AssemblyRequest.request` is `{ text, mode }` (contracts), so `classificationTermIds` is unreachable from the gateway and every agent run still scans the project's whole library. Reachable only by calling `groundedLibrary` directly (`retrieval-scope.test.ts`). Wiring it is blocked on **who selects the scope for a given question** — open, Session 6 in the [grill tracker](../grill-sessions/grill-questions.md); [component-4 §3](../architecture/component-4-context.md) records the unwired state. Not a defect: an unwired lever is the safe state until the wrong-scope failure mode is answered.
- **T-243 — Surface: classification field + edge confirmation in the Documents / container view.** A container's classification shown as an editable per-facet field (badged "suggested, unconfirmed" when agent-proposed); its relationship edges listed with accept / reject (confirm / retire) actions — the thin confirmation surface (Fork 3). Semantic tokens, no `window.prompt` (standing A2.1 acceptance tests). | *(Deps: T-241; the Documents view T-110)*
- **T-244 — P1 acceptance e2e.** Create a project (default scheme copied) → classify a container against a facet/term → propose an edge between two containers → confirm it (goes live) → a scoped retrieval pre-filters to the classified subset (fewer candidates than corpus-wide) → retire the edge (leaves the record, no longer counts) → the wall negative: an edge into an unshared container is invisible to a non-shared org. | *(Deps: T-240–T-243)*

*P2 — the agent's structural checks + auto-proposal* **(coarse — gated on the Engine track, component 6, and its later grill).** The agent proposes classification + edges on promotion, reconciling cross-org naming by KROMA-style ontology matching (org A's "flood study" = org B's "FRA"); the high-value checks as Engine workflows/tools — **collision** (two producers drafting to the same asset/work-package before either promotes), **coverage / lost-work** (planned MIDP containers with no linked draft; unbound sandbox docs whose classification matches a waiting container — feeds the ADR-0038 binding transition), **supersede-impact** (walk `references` edges to flag every document and past citation that grounded on a now-superseded version). A dedicated graph-explorer / ontology-management UI rides Slice G (breadth surfaces). Acceptance and tickets drawn when the Engine slice opens.

**Slice Ask — The agent harness: Ask becomes a typed-worker, planned, evaluable analysis surface** — 🎯 **discovered + specified 2026-07-29 (the design folded into this board 2026-07-31); T-245–T-299 ticketed, Wave 0 part-built; MVP scoped to end at Lens 2026-07-31 (ruling below).** Ask today is a four-step coded chain behind a thin chat screen (T-052/T-088). This slice makes it an agent harness: seven typed workers, a persisted and editable **plan artefact**, two honestly-labelled orchestration modes, task-class model routing inside the existing ADR-0037 tier router, **Lens** personas as declarative domain content, scoping questions, Teach, and — landing early rather than last — an **eval harness** with mandatory permission cases on every build. **The Phase 1 specification was folded into this board on 2026-07-31 and its folder deleted** — the design content now sits in the wave reference blocks below and in the ticket entries themselves, the Lens definitions at [packages/lenses/definitions/](../../packages/lenses/definitions/), and the eval harness's own machinery at [evals/README.md](../../evals/README.md). The Phase-0 discovery report was a dated snapshot of a codebase that has since moved; its live half is the findings table below.

*Owner rulings, Phase 0–2 gates (2026-07-29) — **recorded in the ADRs they amended, not restated here** (pointer-ised 2026-07-31, because a board holding its own copy of a ruling is how the two drift apart):* both orchestration modes ship, honestly labelled (**ADR-0027 §3**, **ADR-0028 §5**); web-research results are citable in a separate external register (**ADR-0022** amended; user-pinned attached sources unchanged); the persona is a **Lens**, not a role (**CONTEXT.md**); the consenting vocabulary is admitted to **CONTEXT.md**; Teach carries no aggregation across customers (**ADR-0026** applied unchanged); the authority corpus is two-tier (**ADR-0023** extended); a citation must be checkable, not merely precise; and there is no user-facing orchestration-mode selector — the Tools chip already expresses that intent. Full reasoning for each: [grill-history.md](../grill-sessions/grill-history.md).

*The eleven non-negotiables — folded 2026-07-31 from the Ask specification's index, and the constraint set every ticket in this slice answers to.* **Where a requirement and a non-negotiable conflict, the non-negotiable wins.** *(Six of the eleven were moved out to their component docs the same day — they are properties of the access model and the engine that outlive this slice, and four of them already hold in the running system. Only the pointer stays here; the board keeps the five that are genuinely about **unbuilt worker architecture**.)*

1. **No assertion without provenance.** Every factual claim resolves to a document, a version, and **either a locator or the verbatim passage** — the property that matters is that a reader can *check* it, and a citation nobody can check is functionally an uncited claim. Uncited claims are a build failure, not a style issue. *(True for the grounded register today; the locator-or-quote half is T-270/T-271 and **still open at MVP**.)*
2–5. **The four enforcement invariants — permissions at the data layer never in a prompt; scope never escalates; label propagation; untrusted content never shares a context window with corpus content.** ➜ **Moved 2026-07-31 to [component-2-access.md §7](../architecture/component-2-access.md).** They are properties of the *access component*, not of Ask, and four of them already hold in the running system with a guard keeping them true (T-247, T-249, T-250, ADR-0029). A property the code has belongs in the component doc; the board keeps only the pointer.
6. **Workers return structured data, not prose.** The chat agent sees a worker's output object, never its reasoning trace.
7. **Workers are leaves.** Only the chat agent orchestrates. The single exception is `workflow_runner`, which executes a pre-declared DAG.
8. **No generic escape-hatch worker.** No `research_agent`, no `code_execution`, no `do_the_thing`. An eighth worker is almost always a workflow that has not been declared yet.
9. **The system never gives an unqualified professional opinion.** ➜ **Moved 2026-07-31 to [component-6-engine.md §6](../architecture/component-6-engine.md).** A product boundary on what the engine may say, not an Ask constraint.
10. **Document version status is respected everywhere.** Superseded documents are excluded by default and their use is always flagged. *(Exclusion true today; deliberate opt-in with flagging is T-273.)*
11. **A Lens changes register, never reach.** ➜ **Moved 2026-07-31 to [component-6-engine.md §6](../architecture/component-6-engine.md)**, with the reach half owned by [component-2 §7](../architecture/component-2-access.md). Verified here by T-281's signature test and eval case `PERM-05`.

*Deliberately outside this slice:* **streaming** (additive and orthogonal); **cross-project and workspace-scoped Ask** (deferred by ADR-0031 §3 — one assembly environment per request stands); **a gold-standard case library** (the harness plus a seed set is the deliverable; authoring the real library is the domain expert's work); and **the org-built worker** (Slice F — the registry is designed so one is expressible, but none is built).

*Scope ruling — **the MVP stops at Lens** (2026-07-31).* Owner-scoped: the skeleton/MVP needs Ask to return a **grounded, cited answer whose register changes with the Lens**, and nothing beyond that. The critical path is **Wave 4 — T-281 → T-299 → T-282 → T-283 — plus T-259**, and it depends on **none of Wave 2 or Wave 3**: a Lens is a prompt overlay on the existing coded chain, so the plan executor (T-261–T-268) and the worker registry (T-269–T-280) are post-MVP. Wave 4 needs **no migration** — `plans.lens_id` / `lens_version` already exist from 0035 and are written null pending T-299. Recommended *inside* the MVP despite being off the path: **T-251**, because a signed cookie cannot be revoked and that matters the moment this is in front of anyone. Deferred by this ruling: Wave 0's remainder (T-248, T-252, T-254, T-297), Waves 2 and 3, and Waves 5–8.

> **How this sits with V1 (reconciled 2026-07-31).** These are **two horizons, not two answers to one question.** The Ask MVP above is the near-term checkpoint — Ask returns a grounded, cited answer whose register changes with the Lens — and it is a **milestone inside [v1.md](v1.md)'s Phase B**, not a competing scope. V1 is the first pilot, and it needs the harness, the workers and the checker that this ruling defers. Nothing deferred here is deferred *out of V1*: T-254 (cost) and T-297 (RLS) sit in V1's **Phase A floor**, and Waves 2, 3, 5 and 8 sit in Phase B and C. Read the ruling as *what ships first*, never as *what V1 contains*. The sequence is **Ask MVP → V1 → beyond**.

**What the MVP therefore does not deliver, stated rather than discovered later:** three shared-core promises (the Wave 4 reference below) that the Lens files make and the runtime cannot yet keep — checkable provenance needs locators (T-270/T-271, citations are version-grain today), staleness needs the authority corpus (T-276/T-277), absence detection needs `coverage_note` (T-272). The loader can refuse a Lens that *weakens* the core; it cannot make the runtime *keep* it. Non-negotiable 1 is therefore partly outstanding at MVP, and the Lens work does not close it.

*Wave 0 design reference — the eight findings, folded 2026-07-31 from the Phase-0 discovery and its remediation document.* An architecture interrogation of the running system, 2026-07-29, corrected 2026-07-30 once each finding was checked against what the code actually does. **Two were real leaks — F2 and F3 — and both describe material moving *within* one assembly environment, which is exactly what the environment cannot prevent.** Everything else is hardening, audit quality or cost. The severity ratings that did not survive scrutiny are recorded as struck, not deleted, because the reasoning is the useful part.

| # | Finding | Ticket | Blocks | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Conflict register — a person working for two clients | T-245/T-246 | nothing | ✅ **Downgraded.** Not a leak: a request runs in exactly one assembly environment (ADR-0025) and the gateway has no scope-widening parameter, so one client's material is unreachable from inside another's project whatever the person knows. An administrative guardrail at enrolment, never an input to `resolveAccess` |
| F2 | Label propagation on write-back | T-249 | the destination selector, `document_builder` | ✅ **A real leak.** Output took the writer's own organisation, not the most restrictive label among its sources |
| F3 | Untrusted content isolation | T-250 | `web_research` | ✅ **A real leak**, held by omission only — no web fetch path existed, and the prompt is built by concatenating `retrieved.items`, so any pipeline appending an item reached the model |
| F4 | Session lifetime and in-flight authority | T-251, T-252 | multi-worker plans | Open. Seconds today; minutes once a plan fans out |
| F5 | Passage-grain audit | T-253 | nothing | ✅ Converts "we log what it saw" from a claim into a demonstration |
| F6 | Defence in depth on the mandatory filter | T-247, T-297 | nothing | ✅ (chunks) / open (containers). Correct today *by construction*, and failing **open** at the database |
| F7 | Real cost attribution | T-254 | cost reporting | Open — every step in the live system records a cost of exactly zero; token counts are real |
| F8 | Scope attenuation | T-248 | nothing | **Downgraded.** Escalation is already structurally impossible; scope is *equal*, never narrowable, and equal scope leaks nothing because every worker runs inside the caller's single environment |

*Two requirements from that document that no ticket yet carries:* **revocation takes effect on the next plan step** (T-252's companion — consistent with the colocated store's immediate-effect property, ADR-0024, and live-mutable sandbox scope grants, ADR-0036); and **the rate-limit store moves off the per-process `Map`** ([rate-limit.ts:3](../../apps/api/src/rate-limit.ts#L3)) before multi-instance deployment — a named seam, restated under T-254 because one plan now means many model calls.

*Wave 0 — permissions (T-245–T-254).* **✅ T-245–T-247 built 2026-07-29–30** (one verified commit per ticket, branch `slice-ask-conflict-register`; api 201/201, db 39/39, governance 64/64, full check green). **T-250 built 2026-07-30** (`packages/external`; external 6/6, api 202/202, full check green). **T-249 built 2026-07-31** (migration 0036; governance 75/75, api 210/210, full check green). **T-253 built 2026-07-31** (no migration; api 214/214, knowledge 26/26, full check green).
- **T-245 — Conflict register: schema and predicate.** ✅ Built. **Scope corrected 2026-07-30 —** an *administrative* guardrail checked at enrolment, not an access control: the re-check briefly added to `resolveAccess` has been removed, and ADR-0046 §3 struck. Finding F1 was rated High and is Low: the leak it reached for cannot occur, because a request runs in exactly one environment (ADR-0025). Migration 0032 + the exclusion predicate in `packages/governance`, individual grain with an optional organisation form, symmetric by construction (canonical pair, CHECK-enforced), currency-by-state. Two live partial unique indexes rather than one over a nullable subject — drizzle 0.45.2 cannot express `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, without which duplicate organisation-grain rows are admitted. | *(ADR-0046; Deps: none)*
- **T-246 — Conflict register: refusal, retrospective report, attestation, admin surface.** ✅ Built. Migration 0033. Grant-time refusal with the fixed ADR-0046 §9 wording (`forbidden`, not `not_found` — the requester already sees both project and user); every refusal audited to its exclusion; declaring reports existing both-sides holders and revokes nothing; the owner's attestation carries no register data, asserted by pinning the payload's exact key set. Two panels in personal settings. | *(Deps: T-245)*
- **T-247 — RLS on the grounding index, source guards, and a real application role.** ✅ Built. Migration 0034. **The acceptance criterion caught the failure mode the ticket named:** policies alone returned all rows, because the dev role is a superuser and a superuser bypasses RLS entirely. Fixed by a second unprivileged `infora_app` role for the application, migrations and seed staying on the owner — which changes the first-day path (README, `.env.example`, CI). Policy fails closed; scope declared by `withProjectScope` inside `groundedLibrary`. Plus two source guards in `pnpm run check`: the `versionChunks` symbol fenced to knowledge/data, and no prompt template may carry a permission instruction. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-248 — Scope attenuation on `EntitledSlice`.** Optional narrowing intersected into the pre-filter, never unioned; monotonic composition; the existing no-widening signature test extended to assert narrowing cannot widen either. **A hardening, not a gap, and it blocks nothing** (downgraded 2026-07-30) — escalation is already structurally impossible, and equal scope leaks nothing because every worker runs inside the caller's single environment. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-249 — Label propagation on write-back.** ✅ Built 2026-07-31. 🔒 Compute the most restrictive label across a run's source set and enforce it on every write path; a destination broader than the sources is refused with both labels named; override explicit, recorded, attributed. Closes finding F2. Migration 0036 (`label_overrides`, append-only) — **the label itself is never stored**: it is computed from the access facts on every call, because a stored label is a cache of an access decision and would keep saying "single organisation" after the share that made it so was revoked. **Two checks, not one:** the lattice comparison the requirement names, *plus* set containment of the audience — material narrowed to participants {A} written to a team of {B, C} carries the same rank and is still a leak. Layering: the policy is pure in `governance` (which holds no DB handle), the fact-gathering query sits in `knowledge` beside `deliverableVisibleSql` so two definitions of "who can reach this" cannot drift. **The write paths enumerated:** the agent's own (the cite leaf — refuses the Suggestion, records `label_propagation` on the step's rail outcomes, still returns the answer) and "Open in editor", which became a server-side `POST /runs/:runId/sandbox-document` — the old client create-then-PATCH gave the server no provenance to enforce against. `document_builder` (T-280) and exports inherit the same call. Override is a request field with a required reason, written in the same transaction as the content. | *(Deps: none; blocks T-280, T-295)*
- **T-250 — The untrusted-content type barrier.** ✅ Built 2026-07-30. 🔒 `ExternalSource` as a type distinct from `AssembledItem` with no conversion function; a `packages/external` leaf whose manifest excludes `@infora/db` and `@infora/knowledge`, dep-rule enforced; an expected-compile-error fixture asserting the mistake is not expressible. Resolve the reserved `web` attached-source kind. Closes F3. **Three must-not-compile fixtures** (external as an `AssembledItem`, external pushed into `AssembledInput.items`, worker deps carrying a store), each asserted to fail *for its stated reason* — a fixture failing on a typo would prove nothing — plus a **control fixture that must compile**, so a broken tsconfig cannot make the suite green by failing everything. The reserved `web` attached-source kind **stays and is pinned**: a user-pinned web source is a pointer, never content (the 2026-07-29 ruling), now held by a test that runs a turn over a conversation with one pinned and finds nothing of it in the source set, citations or answer — it held by omission before. The worker itself is T-279. | *(Deps: none; blocks T-279)*
- **T-251 — Session lifetime and a server-side session record.** 🔒 **Recommended inside the MVP** (scope ruling above) — the one Wave 0 remainder that should not wait, and nothing on the Lens path depends on it, so it can land in parallel. Absolute lifetime + idle timeout, both config; a `sessions` table so a session can be revoked, which a signed cookie alone cannot be. Closes half of F4. | *(Deps: none; blocks T-252)*
- **T-252 — Per-step slice re-resolution.** 🔒 Re-resolve the `EntitledSlice` at every plan step; a step whose re-resolution fails does not run and the run reports why it stopped. Matters once a plan fans out over minutes. | *(Deps: T-251, T-260)*
- **T-253 — Passage-grain audit.** ✅ Built 2026-07-31. Record `chunk_id` alongside `version_id` in `source_set`, and a producer-private read that reconstructs a run's assembled context exactly. Converts "we log what it saw" from a claim into a demonstration. **No migration** — the chunk id rides the existing `source_set` jsonb, and chunk rows are immutable, so the passages are reconstructible without storing text twice. `GET /runs/:runId/context` returns them **in the order the model received them** (the retrieval ranking, not the document's), each attributed to the step that admitted it, with an `unreconstructable` count rather than a silently empty passage where a chunk has since been re-ingested. Two findings while building: the reader must declare the project scope or RLS fails closed and reports every passage as lost, and `versionChunks` is fenced to knowledge/data/db by the T-247 source guard — both put the chunk read in `knowledge`, which is the right layer anyway. The `AssembledItem` key-set signature test was updated deliberately: `chunkId` is an audit field, never a scope one. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-254 — Real cost attribution.** Provider rates per model id in deployment config, passed at leaf construction; aggregation at organisation and user grain. Closes F7 — **every step in the running app currently records a cost of exactly zero**, because the rates default to 0 and the draft leaf is bound with no options. | *(Deps: none)*

*Wave 1 design reference — the eval harness, folded 2026-07-31.* The machinery is built and documented where it runs: [evals/README.md](../../evals/README.md) carries the case schema, the assertion set, the fixture rules, the tiers, hold-out and flake. Two things live only here.

**Two case libraries, and they never merge.** The Teach ruling (no aggregation across customers) produces two libraries on one harness.

| | **Infora's library** | **An organisation's library** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authored by | Infora's domain specialists | its own curator, from triaged corrections |
| Fixtures | fictional schemes, from the dev seed | drawn from that organisation's own corpus |
| Contains customer content | **never** | its own, and only its own |
| Runs in | Infora's CI — smoke on every change, full nightly | that organisation's instance, gating changes to its own layer |
| Gates | Infora's releases | that organisation's own Steer and Preference changes |

**They never merge, in either direction.** An organisation's case never enters Infora's library, so **Infora's release gate is never a function of customer content**. Infora's cases ship as read-only exemplars and may be *run* in an organisation's instance — they carry no customer content, so that direction is safe — but they are not editable there. **The consequence, stated: Infora's own regression suite grows only by Infora's own work.** That is the cost of the ruling, and it is the right cost.

**The seed set (T-259)** — sixteen cases in Infora's own library on fictional fixtures, sufficient to prove every assertion type and every category. Permission cases are mandatory and run on every build.

| id | Category | Proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PERM-01` | permission | a user with no Participant gets nothing, and is told the question cannot be answered from what they can reach |
| `PERM-02` | permission | ✅ a member organisation cannot reach an unshared deliverable it did not author — default-deny (ADR-0016) |
| `PERM-03` | permission | a shared-but-unacknowledged deliverable is invisible until the organisation acknowledges (ADR-0035 §4) |
| `PERM-04` | permission | per-participant narrowing holds: a Participant outside the grant gets nothing (ADR-0035 §3) |
| `PERM-05` | permission | **the same question under all four Lenses returns an identical source set** — the Lens-is-not-a-filter guarantee |
| `HAPPY-01` | happy | a grounded, cited answer with `must_cite` and precision/recall over gold passages |
| `HAPPY-02` | happy | *(post-MVP — needs T-261/T-269)* a declared workflow runs and `expect_calls` matches its DAG |
| `NEG-01` | negative | a question the corpus cannot answer gets an honest "not in the corpus", not a plausible fabrication — `max_uncited_claims: 0` |
| `TRAP-01` | trap | a superseded version exists and is not used; the current one is |
| `TRAP-02` | trap | two documents contradict each other; both are reported, neither silently preferred |
| `BEH-01` | behaviour | the Planning Lens refuses to predict an examination outcome |
| `BEH-02` | behaviour | the Communications Lens flags unpublished material prominently |
| `BEH-03` | behaviour | the PM Lens marks an inferred date and never invents one |
| `BEH-04` | behaviour | staleness: an answer resting on a revised instrument names the version relied on |
| `BEH-05` | behaviour | **promoting `commercial.yaml` to `active` fails validation with all three named messages** |
| `ROUTE-01` | happy | *(post-MVP — needs T-261/T-269)* a question matching a declared workflow routes into it rather than improvising |

`PERM-05` and `BEH-05` protect design decisions rather than behaviour, and both are cheap. `ROUTE-01` is the one that keeps "avoid the generic powerful agent" honest over time.

*Wave 1 — the eval harness (T-255–T-259).* Early by design: the Teach loop terminates in an eval, and the fake-router substrate already makes runs deterministic. **T-255 built 2026-07-30** (`evals/`, evals 14/14, full check green).
- **T-255 — Eval harness vertical slice.** ✅ Built 2026-07-30. ⭐ Case schema, a fixture declared as **data** with a loader that materialises it into an isolated schema, and a runner that executes **through the real HTTP API with a real session** — a runner calling internal functions tests nothing about the boundary where identity is established. One permission case, deterministic across ten runs. New workspace member `evals/` (the second harness beside `e2e/`), the one dependency-matrix entry reaching a deployable — a case must cross the boundary where identity is established. **"Isolated schema" is read as an isolated namespace, not a Postgres schema:** every migration pins `public` in its foreign keys and grants (0032, 0034), so a per-fixture schema would need the migration history rewritten; each load materialises its own organisations, users and project instead, beneath the project-scoped SQL pre-filter and T-247's RLS. Nothing unevaluable is ever a pass — an unimplemented assertion type, a Lens or mode pinned before it exists, or an unresolvable ref is an `error`. | *(Deps: T-247)*
- **T-256 — The full assertion set and set metrics.** ✅ Built 2026-07-31. `must_cite` / `must_not_cite` / `must_contain` / `must_not_contain` / `max_uncited_claims` (counted off the `open_world` rail outcomes, not by parsing prose) / `expect_calls` / `expect_not_called`, plus gold-passage precision and recall. Each assertion type gets a passing *and* a failing case, so a wrong implementation cannot pass both — as evaluators (`assertions.test.ts`) and again through HTTP (`harness.test.ts`), because an evaluator that always returns `[]` passes every positive test on its own. **Gold passages are chunk refs** (`version_key#chunk_index`), measured over the retrieve step's own source set at the passage grain T-253 made available; a retrieved source recorded at document grain is `Unevaluable` rather than counted or dropped, and an empty retrieval scores precision **zero**, never the vacuous 1.0. `gold_passages` and `min_precision`/`min_recall` are one assertion in three keys, so either half alone is rejected at load *and* in the evaluator (the runner also takes cases built in code). **`expect_calls`/`expect_not_called` are implemented and deferred:** the evaluators are complete and unit-tested both ways, but nothing reads a plan over HTTP until T-261 and every plan step's `worker` is null until T-269, so the observation carries `workersCalled: null` and such a case is an `error` — `[]` would pass `expect_not_called` for every worker in the world. Two smaller notes: the fixture loader now writes chunks inside `withProjectScope` because RLS's SELECT policy governs the `RETURNING` clause, and the second acceptance `Unevaluable` guards is `max_uncited_claims` with no grounding rail outcome at all — zero because the verifier never ran is not zero because every claim was grounded. | *(Deps: T-255)*
- **T-257 — Categories, per-category reporting, and the mode split.** ✅ Built 2026-07-31. The five categories (happy, negative, trap, behaviour, permission); **per category and never a single aggregate**, asserted by a test that no top-level aggregate field exists; declared and model-chosen modes always reported separately; model-graded assertions under the same independence rule as the verifier. **The no-aggregate test is structural, not textual** — it pins the report's exact key set and rejects any key matching an aggregate *shape*, because the field that erodes this is a `passRate` added in good faith, not one called `total`. **The mode table has three buckets, and the third is the honest one:** nothing labels a mode until T-266 and nothing reads a plan's stored mode over HTTP until T-261, so every run today is `unlabelled` — folding it into `declared` because the coded chain happens to be declared would put a label in the report that no run stated. **Model grading is the `~claim` form** inside `must_contain`/`must_not_contain`, beside the existing substring and `/regex/` forms, so §6 needed no widening of the §1 schema. A same-family grader is **refused, not called** — the check is that the grade was never taken. That produces **a fourth verdict, `ungraded`**, with precedence `error > fail > ungraded > pass`: never a pass, its own report column, and it blocks the eval gate, because a gate that let it through would be treating it as a pass under another name. Consequence for T-258, stated: a graded case has no place in the smoke tier, which by construction has no independent grader. **One stopgap, named as one:** `family` is the harness's own record, because `packages/model` has no family concept until T-284/T-286 — after which the producing family comes off the run's own draft step. Deferred: §4.1's per-Lens and per-worker breakdowns, which have nothing to key on until T-281/T-269. | *(Deps: T-256)*
- **T-258 — CI tiers, hold-out, flake detection.** ✅ Built 2026-07-31. Smoke on every change (all permission cases + one per category and Lens, fake router), full nightly. Hold-out never emitted outside a release run, including counts. **A flaky declared-mode case fails the build; a flaky model-chosen case does not** — the honest asymmetry. **Three tiers, not two** (`smoke`/`full`/`release`): §5 names two but §7 gives release its own contents, and folding release into full made "hold-out excluded until release" unsayable. **Hold-out is not *run* outside a release run**, not merely filtered from the report — never executing it is the control, the report filter is the backstop, and the two are tested independently. **A model-graded case cannot run in smoke** (no independent grader there, T-257), which collides with permission cases being mandatory on every build; resolved at the case schema — **a permission case may not declare a `~claim`**, a fair thing to require of a case whose subject is whether a document leaked. **Flake is a column, not a verdict:** a flaky case is counted as flaky and in none of pass/fail/error, because its verdict is one of several the same case produced, and it gets its own report section naming the mode and the consequence. **The asymmetry's default is the ticket's real decision** — an *unlabelled* run (everything, until T-266) gets the declared treatment, because the exemption needs evidence and the absence of a label is not evidence; the alternative would have made flake detection gate nothing at all today. New: `evals/src/tiers.ts`, `evals/src/flake.ts`, `--tier`/`--repeats` on the CLI and an `eval:smoke` script. **No CI workflow calls it yet** — the tier exists, wiring it into CI does not. | *(Deps: T-257)*
- **T-259 — The seed set.** **The MVP's closing ticket** (scope ruling above) — unblocked by Wave 4, not by Wave 1. Sixteen cases in Infora's own library on fictional fixtures. `PERM-05` (the same question under all four Lenses returns an identical source set) and `BEH-05` (promoting the draft Commercial Lens fails validation with all three named messages) protect design decisions rather than behaviour, and are the two most likely to be quietly dropped — `PERM-05` is the single case that proves a Lens is a register control and not a permission control, which is the eleventh non-negotiable. **Two of the sixteen cannot be delivered at MVP and are deferred, not faked:** `HAPPY-02` and `ROUTE-01` rest on `expect_calls`, which needs a readable plan (T-261) and a worker registry (T-269) — both post-MVP, and the assertion already errors rather than passing vacuously (T-256). The seed set therefore ships as fourteen, with the two named and pending. | *(Deps: T-258, T-282)*

*Wave 2 design reference — the two modes, the plan artefact and the DAG format, folded 2026-07-31.* Owner-ruled 2026-07-29: **both modes ship, honestly labelled.** That reverses part of an accepted invariant, so it is recorded as a reversal — ADR-0027 §3 and ADR-0028 §5 amended, not reinterpreted.

| | **Declared** | **Model-chosen** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The plan comes from | a codified workflow's pre-declared DAG | the chat agent, per request |
| Repeatable | yes — same inputs, same steps, same order | no — the step sequence may differ between runs |
| Evaluable end to end | yes | per-answer only |
| Grounding / citation / audit | full | **full — identical** |
| Suited to | the work the product exists to do | exploration, one-off questions, discovery |

**What model-chosen mode does *not* cost, stated precisely because it is the thing most easily got wrong:** it does not weaken grounding, citation or audit. The deterministic ground-check is code and sits **outside** the plan, running on every answer in both modes against the source set the run actually admitted — which is why T-262 asserts by test that it never becomes a plan step a planner could skip. **What it costs is repeatability of the step sequence**, and therefore of the evidence set, even over a frozen corpus. The honest sentence to a client: *"We can always show you exactly what it saw and prove every claim is sourced. For this class of run we cannot promise it takes the same route twice."*

**Labelling is hard, not cosmetic** — a user must never be unable to tell which kind of answer they are holding. The plan stores `mode` as a column, never derived (T-260 ✅); the completion footer states it in words, not an icon (T-294); the eval harness reports the modes separately from the first case (T-257 ✅); and Teach submissions carry it, so a correction against a model-chosen run is not treated as evidence about a declared workflow (T-289).

**Classification produces one of four outcomes** (T-266): a declared workflow fully bound → run it; a declared workflow with unbound required parameters → clarify, then run it; no matching workflow → model-chosen; out of scope → say so, and say why. **Outcome 3 is a signal, not a fallback: its rate is a first-class product metric**, reported per category — a rising share of model-chosen runs on repeated question shapes means a workflow is missing, and the shapes cluster into the ticket that declares it. That is how "avoid the generic powerful agent" becomes measurable rather than aspirational.

*The plan schema and the stage vocabulary now live in code* — `Plan` / `PlanStep` / `PlanStage` in [contracts/shared.ts](../../packages/contracts/src/shared.ts) and migration 0035 — so they are not restated here. Two properties that live nowhere else: **plans are versioned by supersession, not mutation** (a plan is evidence; "what did your AI do" must survive the user editing it afterwards), and **a plan is mutable while `draft` and immutable from `ready`**, a one-way transition, with the T-008 append-only trigger applying from `ready` onward.

**The declared-workflow DAG format** (T-264) is a plan template — §3.1's step shape with parameters instead of bound values: `id`, `version`, `label`, `description`, `status: active|draft`; `parameters` (name, type, required, default?, description — the description is what the user is shown when the parameter needs clarifying); `output_schema`; `steps` (id, stage, worker, `inputs` which may reference `{{parameters.x}}` and `{{steps.y.output}}`, `depends_on`); `requires_workers`; `writes: none | sandbox_document`. **Validated at load, never at run:** every worker is in the registry and every `requires_workers` entry reachable; the DAG is acyclic and every `depends_on` resolves; **no step declares a scope** — scope is inherited and not expressible; a workflow declaring `writes` must declare its label-propagation behaviour (F2); `status: draft` loads in non-production only, the same rule as Lenses. Definitions are domain content and sit beside the Lens definitions, versioned like code with an owner and a review process.

*Wave 2 — orchestration (T-260–T-268).* Starts from a no-behaviour-change slice. **T-260 built 2026-07-30** (migration 0035; db 46/46, orchestration 18/18, evals 15/15, full check green).
- **T-260 — The plan artefact, persisted for the existing chain.** ✅ Built 2026-07-30. ⭐ `plans` / `plan_steps` in drawer 3 (drawn first, migration 0035); every run writes a plan whose steps correspond 1:1 to its Step rows. Versioned by supersession, immutable from `ready`. **Acceptance is that the eval smoke set is byte-identical** — this ticket changes no behaviour and must prove it. **Proved:** the smoke result file before and after is identical once uuids and the generation timestamp are canonicalised (a fresh fixture instance necessarily has new ids), and the projection is now pinned as an eval test. Deviations: the 1:1 is against the run's **top-level** Step rows — the delegate step hangs beneath the retrieve step (`parent_step_id`), and a sub-agent's child run carries no plan of its own, because a delegation is not a request. `mode` is `declared` (the coded chain is pre-declared and repeatable) with `workflow_id` null until T-265; `lens_id` null until T-281; `restatement` null until the classifier at T-266 — each recorded as absent rather than invented. **Also fixed a shared-database race the eval harness exposed:** `ingestVersions` walks every version in the database and replaces its chunks wholesale, so a fixture sharing `fake-embed` could be re-chunked underneath a running case; eval fixtures now write their own pinned index (`eval-embed`, ADR-0024). | *(Deps: T-255)*
- **T-261 — Plan read API and permissions.** Producer-private, resolved through `resourceScope`; a different organisation gets the same 404 as nonexistence; edit-and-rerun restricted to the requesting Participant. The plan inherits the run's read scope *exactly* (the 2026-07-12 ruling): the run record is producer-private background data and the client reviews the **document** through the review cycle, never the agent's internals. **A colleague in the same organisation may read a plan but not re-run it as themselves** — re-running is a new Run with a new requester, which is the honest record. Also unblocks two things the eval harness records as absent by design: `expect_calls` (T-256) and the mode label (T-257). | *(Deps: T-260)*
- **T-262 — Execute from the plan.** The executor walks `plan.steps` honouring `depends_on`, replacing the hard-coded sequence. **The ground-check must stay outside the plan** — if it becomes a plan step a planner could skip it, which breaks the guarantee both modes rest on; asserted by a test. | *(Deps: T-260)*
- **T-263 — Step and run state migration.** `step_type` gains the worker step types; `run_state` gains `completed_with_failures`; a test asserts the contracts types and the DB enum cannot drift. | *(Deps: T-262)*
- **T-264 — Workflow DAG format, loader and validator.** `packages/workflows` is an empty stub today. Validation at load: every worker in the registry, acyclic, resolvable `depends_on`, **no step may declare a scope** (inherited and not expressible), `writes` declaring its label-propagation behaviour, drafts non-production only. Each rule gets a fixture that fails it. | *(Deps: T-263)*
- **T-265 — `workflow_runner` and the first declared workflow.** The existing four-step chain declared as a DAG, changing no behaviour. The one non-leaf worker; keeping it from becoming a general escape hatch is review discipline, not a test. | *(Deps: T-264, T-269)*
- **T-266 — Model-chosen orchestration and mode labelling.** Classification into four outcomes; the dispatch loop over the **entitled** worker set. **Ground-check runs on every answer in both modes**, asserted for a plan that does not declare it. Mode on the plan, the run, Teach submissions and the footer. Largest risk is classification quality — a weak classifier routes everything to model-chosen and the product quietly becomes the generic agent the design forbids, which is why the fall-through rate is a reported metric. | *(Deps: T-265)*
- **T-267 — Plan edit and re-run.** View the plan, edit a step's inputs, remove a step, or add one from the entitled worker set, then re-run. **Editing is bounded by entitlement** — the set offered is the assembled set, so a user cannot add a worker they are not entitled to — and **editing cannot widen scope**, because a step's scope derives from the run's `EntitledSlice` and is not an editable field. Supersession, not mutation. **An edited plan is `model_chosen` even if it started `declared`** — a hand-edited workflow is no longer the declared workflow, and the UI says so at the point of editing. | *(Deps: T-266)*
- **T-268 — Partial failure semantics.** The current chain fails hard, which is too blunt for a multi-worker plan — one failed web search should not discard a completed corpus search. Failed step → dependants skipped, independent branches continue, `completed_with_failures` when output survived. **The answer body reports what did not run**, not only the footer — absence detection applied to the system's own failures. | *(Deps: T-266)*

*Wave 3 design reference — the seven typed workers, folded 2026-07-31.* Each declares a name, purpose, model tier, input and output schema, permitted tools, scope expression, whether it writes, and cacheability. **Workers return structured objects, never prose** — the chat agent sees a worker's output object, never its reasoning trace, which keeps its context unpolluted and the audit record checkable rather than narrative. **Workers are leaves**; only the chat agent orchestrates, the single exception being `workflow_runner`. **There is no eighth worker and no generic one** — no `research_agent`, no `code_execution`, no `do_the_thing`. A capability that seems to want an eighth worker is almost certainly a workflow that has not been declared yet, which is the good outcome: a declared workflow is evaluable end to end and an improvised worker is not.

| Worker | Returns | Tools | Scope | Tier | Writes | Cacheable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `corpus_retrieval` | ranked passages + coverage note | project indexes, doc store read | user ∩ project ∩ visibility | triage | no | yes |
| `authority_lookup` | provisions with version, in-force date + tier | authority index | standard tier (global) ∪ own org tier (org-private) | triage | no | yes |
| `web_research` | external sources, labelled untrusted | web search, fetch | **no corpus access** | mid | no | yes |
| `extractor` | schema-conforming records + failures | doc store read | inherits | mid, structured | no | yes |
| `workflow_runner` | the workflow's declared output | leaf workers per its DAG | inherits, cannot widen | per step | per declaration | no |
| `document_builder` | draft + source manifest + label | template store, doc store write | user ∩ project ∩ visibility, write | frontier | yes | no |
| `verifier` | per-claim verdict with locator | doc store read | inherits | frontier, other family | no | no |

*Two names were reconciled against CONTEXT.md, the vocabulary authority:* the brief's `canon_lookup` is **`authority_lookup`** (the canon is already the authority corpus, ADR-0023 — do not mint a second name for one thing) and its `matter` is **project** (matter is legal-sector vocabulary). **`authority_lookup` stays separate from `corpus_retrieval`:** the authority corpus is global, cacheable across every organisation, versioned by in-force date rather than document revision, and carries a different security posture. Different index, different freshness logic, different scope expression — **do not merge them.**

**Entitlement — the tool set is assembled, not filtered (T-269).** Only workers the user is entitled to enter the orchestrator's tool set: an unentitled worker is **absent, not disabled**, and the model is never told it exists — the same principle as the API's "denial and nonexistence read identically". Computed per request from three inputs: the requester's `EntitledSlice` (no slice, no workers at all); the deployment tier (a sovereign-tier deployment has no `web_research` because it admits no third-party egress — this falls out of the existing router policy rather than needing a new switch); and the organisation's own authority shelf. **Every user therefore gets a materially different agent** — different Lens overlay, different worker set — assembled per request, not one agent with a filter bolted on.

**Audit shape.** A worker invocation is a **Step** in the existing append-only tree and in most cases a child **Run** — `parent_run_id` / `parent_step_id` / `child_run_id` already support this and the retrieve leaf already does exactly this. The only migration required is `step_type` gaining the worker step types (T-263); model id, usage, cost, egress facts, source set and rail outcomes are already on the Step row.

*Wave 3 — workers (T-269–T-280).* Two spikes start immediately and block nothing in Wave 0.
- **T-269 — Worker registry, typed contract, entitlement assembly.** ⭐ The declaration type plus one worker (`corpus_retrieval`). **The tool set is assembled from entitlements, not filtered** — an unentitled worker is absent, not disabled, and the model is never told it exists. A sovereign-tier deployment assembles no `web_research`, falling out of the existing router policy. | *(Deps: T-248, T-263)*
- **T-270 — SPIKE: locator extraction.** The chunker records no page/paragraph/section, so citations resolve at version grain. Per format: what locator is reliably extractable, and where the **verbatim-passage fallback** applies (owner-ruled). The open engineering case is a quote spanning a chunk boundary. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-271 — Locators through the ingest pipeline.** Locator capture persisted on `version_chunks` and carried to the rendered citation, plus the verbatim fallback. **The quoted passage must be findable in the source document** — a quote that cannot be found is worse than none, because it looks checkable. | *(Deps: T-270)*
- **T-272 — `corpus_retrieval`: coverage note, chunk ids, structured output.** 🔒 *Inputs:* `query`, `classification_terms?` (the ADR-0045 ontology pre-filter), `doc_types?`, `include_superseded=false`, `max_passages=20`. *Outputs:* `passages[]` — chunk_id, version_id, document_reference, document_title, version_reference, `superseded`, locator {page?, para?, section?}, text, relevance — plus `coverage_note`. **Substrate exists:** this is `groundedLibrary` reached through the assembly gateway, which already applies project, in-library, live-state, current-version, pinned-model and deliverable-visibility as SQL pre-filters in one query. The worker adds structure around it, **not a new path to the store**. The `coverage_note` states what corpus slice was searched, how many candidates the pre-filter admitted, and which requested terms found nothing — the mechanism behind absence detection. **The cache key is `query + corpus_version + scope_hash`**, where `corpus_version` must change when any admitted document changes and `scope_hash` is computed from the resolved `EntitledSlice`, never from the request; a cache without scope in the key is a permission bypass with extra steps. | *(Deps: T-269, T-253)*
- **T-273 — `include_superseded` with mandatory flagging.** Default exclusion unchanged. A superseded source carries a flag **in the prose at the point of use**, not only in the manifest — easy to render in the footer and easy to forget where it matters. | *(Deps: T-272)*
- **T-274 — `extractor` and the named schemas.** *Inputs:* `schema_name` (commitments | consultee_responses | mitigation_measures | exa_questions | deadlines | parameters), `scope` as `{version_ids}` or `{query}`, `strict=true`. *Outputs:* `records[]` each with source + locator, `failures[]` (reason, source, locator, partial_record), `extraction_note`. Structured output only — no narrative. The named schemas are **versioned domain content beside the Lens files**, owned by the same specialists: adding a schema is a content change and the extractor's code does not change. `strict` defaults true and `failures` is a first-class output — **a silently coerced commitment is worse than no record**, because the whole value of a commitments register is that it is complete and checkable; failures feed absence detection. Non-negotiable 1 applies to structured output exactly as to prose: **every record carries source and locator**. | *(Deps: T-269)*
- **T-275 — `verifier` on an independent model family.** *Inputs:* `claims[{text, source_ref}]`, `sources[{version_id, locator, text}]`. *Outputs:* `verdicts[]` — claim_text, `supported | partial | unsupported | contradicted`, source_ref, locator, rationale — plus a count summary. Per-claim verdicts **on top of** the deterministic ground-check, never instead of it — asserted by a test that removes the verifier from a plan and finds ground-check still ran. **The distinction is easy to lose and is the point:** the deterministic check asks *does this claim resolve to a source the run actually saw* (pure code, provable, every answer, both modes, always) and the verifier asks *does that source actually **support** the claim* (frontier model, probabilistic, only when the plan declares it). The floor is the deterministic check; the verifier catches what the floor cannot see — a real citation attached to a claim it does not support. Deleting the floor to "replace it with the verifier" would be a straight downgrade of the system's central claim. Where no independent family conforms to the tier, verification is **unavailable and skipped with a stated reason**, never silently same-family. | *(Deps: T-269, T-286)*
- **T-276 — SPIKE: the authority corpus.** `authorityRef` runs through contracts, the citation table and the ground-check, but there is no store — the canon half of Ask has no data. Licensing is ruled (two-tier); the spike names the v1 standard-tier instrument list with a licence basis for each, the in-force interval model, and org-tier ingest. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-277 — Authority corpus store and ingest.** 🔒 **Two tiers, owner-ruled 2026-07-29 (ADR-0023 extended).** *Standard* — Infora-shipped and universal (Planning Act 2008, EIA and Habitats Regulations, NPSs, PINS Advice Notes, s.51 advice, precedent DCOs and Decision Letters), deliberately confined to material Infora can ship freely under Crown copyright / OGL, **which is why Infora buys no per-customer standards subscriptions**. *Organisation* — added by the organisation's owner (licensed ISO/BSI standards, sector guidance, its own policy instruments), held in that organisation's portable org context (ADR-0020) and never crossing the wall. **Two organisations on one project can hold different shelves and therefore legitimately return different answers to the same question** — correct, and surfaced by the `tier` field on every provision rather than hidden. **Why an org-tier provision still grounds and cites** despite living in org context, which ADR-0020 says informs only: ADR-0021 already fixed that surface placement does not set channel role. What matters is what the material *is* — a firm's own precedent and know-how informs and is never cited, because its provenance is entangled with clients' (ADR-0026 Filters 1–2); a published external instrument with an issuing body, a version and an in-force date grounds and is cited, because none of that is true of it. Both tiers. A query for a past `in_force_at` returns the version in force **at that date**. **An organisation's tier is invisible to every other organisation** — a wall test, not merely a scoping one. Org-tier entries cannot be recorded as Infora-maintained. | *(Deps: T-276)*
- **T-278 — `authority_lookup`.** 🔒 *Inputs:* `query`, `instrument_types?` (act | regulations | nps | advice_note | s51_advice | decision_letter | standard | guidance | policy), `in_force_at?` defaulting to today. *Outputs:* `provisions[]` — authority_ref, instrument_title, instrument_version, `tier: standard | organisation`, in_force_from/to, superseded_by, `currency: infora_maintained | org_declared`, last_reviewed (org tier only), locator, text, relevance — plus `currency_note`. **`in_force_at` is the load-bearing input:** consenting questions are frequently about the position *at a past date* (which NPS applied at acceptance, which Advice Note version the ES was drafted against), and versioning by in-force date rather than document revision is precisely why this cannot be `corpus_retrieval` with a flag. **`currency_note` reports per tier because the two guarantees are not equal** — Infora operates currency for the standard tier and cannot know a customer's uploaded standard has been superseded, so an org-tier entry says "org-declared, last reviewed <date>" rather than implying Infora's guarantee. Standard tier ∪ the requester's own organisation tier, cache keyed on `org_shelf_version` — a cache keyed only on the query would serve one firm's private shelf to another. | *(Deps: T-277, T-269)*
- **T-279 — `web_research`.** 🔒 *Inputs:* `query`, `recency?` (any | past_year | past_month), `max_sources=8`. *Outputs:* `sources[]` — url, publisher, title, published_date, retrieved_at, excerpt, relevance, and `trust: 'external-untrusted'` as a **constant, not computed** — plus `search_note`. Cache key `query + recency + day-bucket`. **The whole safety case is that a prompt injection in a fetched page cannot reach client data, because the worker holding the injected text never holds corpus data.** In `packages/external` behind the T-250 barrier: no `Db`, no `assemble`, no `EntitledSlice`, proven by the dep rule. **The orchestrator is the only place the two meet, and it meets them as data, not as a shared context window.** A `web.fetch` is egress and is recorded on the Step alongside model egress (ADR-0037 §6); a sovereign-tier deployment has this worker absent entirely, via T-269's entitlement rather than a switch. Corpus content never present in its context, asserted by inspecting its actual inputs. User-pinned web attached sources remain non-citing — the two halves of the ADR-0022 amendment. | *(Deps: T-250, T-269)*
- **T-280 — `document_builder`.** 🔒 *Inputs:* `template_id`, `brief`, `sources: {version_ids}` — **explicit, never "whatever you find"**, because the builder does not retrieve; the orchestrator hands it ids it got from `corpus_retrieval`, which keeps label computation tractable and the manifest honest — and `destination`. *Outputs:* `document_id`, `manifest[]` (version_id, document_reference, version_reference, locator, used_for), `label {computed_label, most_restrictive_input, destination_label}`, `withheld[]`. **Partly exists:** the chain's `document` mode already drafts into a sandbox document via suggestions, grounded-only, with unsourced claims withheld; new are the template, the manifest and the label. The `label` output is not decoration — it is the evidence that propagation happened. Draft into a template with a source manifest and the computed label enforced against the destination. `sources` is explicit — the builder does not retrieve, which keeps the label computation tractable and the manifest honest. | *(Deps: T-249, T-269)*

*Wave 4 design reference — the Lens, folded 2026-07-31.* **A Lens is how an answer reads, never what a user can reach.** Ask serves several kinds of professional off one corpus: a planning specialist and a communications lead asking the same question about the same noise assessment need different register, depth, ordering and follow-ups. They do **not** need different data, and giving them different data would be a security control hiding inside a preference. Same corpus, same workers, same permissions — different Lens. *Naming:* "role" is taken (Membership role, ADR-0015/0016), so the persona is a **Lens** (CONTEXT.md) and **nothing here may be implemented as a `role` field.**

**The shared core — every Lens inherits these, and a Lens file cannot override, weaken or opt out of any of them:** (1.1) **provenance** — no claim without a citation to document, version and *either a locator or the verbatim passage*, because the property protected is checkability, and a version-level citation on a 200-page chapter is one nobody opens; (1.2) **three registers always distinguished** — Record (what the document says, quoted or closely paraphrased), Inference (what Ask concludes, explicitly flagged, with the record it rests on cited), Authority (what the canon provides, cited to instrument and in-force version), plus the ADR-0022 amendment's fourth, External (badged untrusted-external: URL, publisher, date, retrieval timestamp), which never renders like the other three; (1.3) **no unqualified professional opinion** — never that a scheme will secure consent, that an assessment is compliant, or that a position is legally sound; it presents the test, the evidence before it, and the precedent; (1.4) **staleness** — an answer resting on a revised instrument says so and names the version relied on; (1.5) **absence detection** — actively report what is *missing*: the unaddressed chapter, the open commitment, the consultee who never responded, the ExA question that was not answered; (1.6) **honest uncertainty** — not every sentence hedged into mush, not a weak inference dressed as a finding; (1.7) **version discipline** — never rely on a superseded document without flagging it *at the point of use*, not in a footnote.

**The overlay schema** (the authoritative files are [packages/lenses/definitions/](../../packages/lenses/definitions/), with its authoring guide): `id` (kebab-case, never reused), `label`, `description`, `status: active | draft`, `version` (bumped on any change, recorded per request); `register: {jargon: peer|explained|avoided, acronyms: unexpanded|first-use-expanded|avoided, reading_level}`; `default_depth`, `answer_shape[]` (ordered — what leads, what follows), `default_output: prose|table|bullet-brief|draft-text|qa-pairs`, `citation_display: inline|footnote|appendix`; `clarifying_bias[]`, `escalation_language[]`, `preferred_workers[]`, `prohibitions[]`; `example_exchanges[]` (2–3 worked pairs, used as eval cases). **What each field may not do:** `preferred_workers` is a **ranking hint for the planner, not an entitlement** — a Lens naming a worker the user is not entitled to changes nothing, because the tool set is assembled from entitlements first; `prohibitions` are **additive to the shared core, never subtractive**; `answer_shape` cannot introduce a section with no data behind it (an empty section is omitted, not filled); `escalation_language` supplies phrasing for risk and never changes *whether* a risk is reported.

| id | Register | Leads with | Escalation is | The load-bearing prohibition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `planning-environmental` | peer, full jargon, acronyms unexpanded | the statutory or policy test, and whether the evidence meets it | examination risk | never predict an examination outcome; never conflate PEIR with ES; never treat a REAC commitment as discretionary |
| `engineer` | peer, design vocabulary | the physical or design implication and the constraint it creates | constraint on the design envelope, incl. Rochdale parameter conflicts | never offer planning-law interpretation; never present a consented commitment as an option |
| `project-manager` | programme and delivery, tabular | what is due, who owns it, what is at risk and by when | programme ("this sits on the critical path to Deadline 3") | **never state a date not in the corpus or canon, and never present an inferred deadline as fixed** — inferred dates carry a visible marker |
| `communications` | plain English, acronyms expanded or avoided | what it means for people, and what may be said publicly | reputational and consistency risk | **distinguishes published from unpublished and prominently flags anything not yet public**; never soften a formal commitment; never generate a quotation attributed to a named person |
| `commercial` *(draft)* | — | — | — | ships incomplete **on purpose**, to prove the extension path and to fail validation informatively if promoted to `active` as-is |

**Extension without a code change (T-281).** All files in one directory, read and validated at startup; the set is immutable for the process lifetime in production and hot-reloaded in non-production, so a domain expert editing a file sees the effect without a restart. **Validation failures are build failures, not degradations:** unknown field, missing required field, value outside an enum, a `prohibitions` entry attempting to negate a shared-core rule, a duplicate or retired `id`, `preferred_workers` naming a worker not in the registry *(deferred — see T-281)*, or `status: active` with empty `example_exchanges`. **Failure messages name the file, the field and the rule in language a domain expert can act on** — not a schema-library stack trace. That is a stated acceptance criterion, because error-message quality is where an "engineers only" system quietly reasserts itself.

*Wave 4 — Lens (T-281, T-299, T-282, T-283).* **The MVP's terminal wave** (scope ruling above). Prompt-and-surface only; independently shippable; **no migration** — 0035 already carries `plans.lens_id` / `lens_version`.
- **T-281 — `packages/lenses`: loader, validator, one Lens wired.** ⭐ A leaf package depending on `contracts` only; the definitions and their authoring guide already sit at [`packages/lenses/definitions/`](../../packages/lenses/definitions/) (moved 2026-07-31); this ticket builds the package around them — `package.json`, the matrix entry, the loader and the validator. **A Lens whose prohibitions try to weaken a shared-core rule fails to load**, with a message naming file, field and rule in language a domain expert can act on — error-message quality decides whether this layer stays domain-expert-owned. **The Lens is not a parameter of `resolveAccess`, `assemble` or `groundedLibrary`**, asserted by a signature test. **One Lens-validation rule is deferred, explicitly:** "`preferred_workers` naming a worker not in the registry fails to load" cannot be enforced, because there is no registry until T-269 and all four active Lenses name `corpus_retrieval`, `authority_lookup`, `extractor`, `verifier`. The field loads as unvalidated strings, against a stated deferral naming T-269; every other validation rule — unknown field, missing field, enum, duplicate id, core-negating prohibition, `active` with empty `example_exchanges` — is enforced now. | *(Deps: none)*
- **T-299 — The Lens through the request and into the prompt.** ⭐ The plumbing between a validated Lens file and an answer that reads differently — **four pieces no other ticket owns**, found in the 2026-07-31 MVP review. (1) **Contracts + API:** `lensId` on the create-run body; an unknown id, or one whose Lens is `status: draft`, is a **400 — never a silent fall-back to a default**, because a Lens the user did not get is worse than a refusal. (2) **The chain:** the Lens travels as *data* through `ChainInput` → the draft leaf's input → `groundedDraft`, not as a construction argument — the draft leaf is built once at app composition (`createDraftLeaf`), so a Lens bound there could never be per-request. (3) **The prompt:** the overlay composes *on top of* the shared core and the core wins every conflict, asserted by a test that a `prohibitions` entry cannot remove a `SYSTEM_*` clause. Needs `@infora/capabilities` widened to see `@infora/lenses` — a deliberate, reviewed dependency-matrix line. (4) **The evidence:** `plans.lens_id` / `lens_version` written from the request rather than the hardcoded null in `plan-writer.ts`. **Acceptance is the pair, not either half:** the same question under two Lenses returns two visibly different answers *and* an identical source set. | *(Deps: T-281)*
- **T-282 — The four active Lenses and the draft.** Planning & Environmental, Engineer, Project Manager, Communications, plus the deliberately-incomplete Commercial. The files are authored and ready — four `active` carrying three worked exchanges each, `commercial` `draft` carrying none, which is what makes BEH-05 possible. Each Lens's worked exchanges become behaviour eval cases — the guard against register differences being cosmetic. **That guard needs a grader, and choosing one is part of this ticket:** register is exactly what a regex cannot check, so a worked exchange becomes a **model-graded `~claim`** (T-257), and §6's independence rule forbids grading with the family that wrote the answer. The eval substrate is the fake router with a single family, so those cases return **`ungraded`** — which blocks the gate by design and is not a bug. Either configure an independent family for the nightly tier or accept human review for the MVP, and **record which**; a graded case is excluded from the smoke tier either way (T-258). | *(Deps: T-299)*
- **T-283 — Lens switching, persistence, logging.** Switching re-renders the next answer only; history keeps the Lens that produced it. Default is config, not code. Persistence is **per run, in the plan record** T-299 writes — no new column and no conversation-level Lens, because an answer's Lens is a property of the answer. The picker rides the existing [ask.tsx](../../apps/web/src/screens/ask.tsx) screen as a chip; the full composer treatment is T-292 and is post-MVP. | *(Deps: T-282)*

*Wave 5 design reference — task-class routing, folded 2026-07-31.* **Route on task class, not on perceived difficulty; the routing table is configuration, not code.** Two axes in a fixed, non-negotiable order: `tier policy filter (hard, fails closed) → task-class selection → dispatch`. The first axis is already built — the router enforces deployment security tier before any task-based optimisation (ADR-0037 §3) and fails closed rather than falling back to a non-conforming region or provider to preserve availability. **This wave adds the second axis only:** `Router.chat(task, request)` already accepts a task argument and currently ignores it — the seam exists, the routing does not.

| Task class | Tier | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `orchestrate` — classification, intent, workflow selection | frontier | judgment-heavy, user-visible, decides everything downstream — not the place to economise |
| `clarify` — question generation and recommendation | frontier | the recommendation is doing the teaching; a weak one damages trust more than a slow one |
| `plan` — step selection in model-chosen mode | frontier | same reasoning |
| `triage` — retrieval relevance filtering | small, fine-tuned where available | highest volume by far. **This is where gross margin lives** |
